item.title: master sheet
item.description: An extensive master list of English language learning resources organized by skill area: exam preparation (Cambridge English, FCE, CAE), reading comprehension, grammar practice, dictionaries and translators, vocabulary building apps (Quizlet, Memrise, Duolingo), podcasts for listening practice, and pronunciation tools. All resources are free and suitable for teen and adult learners from intermediate to advanced levels.

item.title: Goo goo go go?
item.description: Young English learners pronouncing ‘so’ as /suː/ (like ’to’ and ‘do’) instead of /səʊ/ reveals how children naturally generalize pronunciation patterns, even when those generalizations conflict with standard rules.

item.title: Interesting Words and Phrases 6
item.description:
Burgeon - Begin to grow or increase rapidly; flourish.

Culture - The arts and other manifestations of human intellectual achievement regarded collectively.

Collectivism - The practice or principle of giving a group priority over each individual in it.

Dualism - The division of something conceptually into two opposed or contrasted aspects, or the state of being so divided

Individualism - A social theory favouring freedom of action for individuals over collective or state control.

item.title: Interesting Words and Phrases 5
item.description:
Exemption - This is a deduction allowed by law to reduce the amount of income that would otherwise be taxed. There are two types offered by the IRS: personal exemptions and dependent exemptions. Deduction - This is any item or expenditure subtracted from gross income to reduce the amount of income subject to income tax. This is also referred to as an “allowable deduction”. Dependent - A dependent is a person who entitles a taxpayer to claim dependent-related tax benefits that reduce that amount of tax that taxpayer owes. Draconian - (relating to or of laws or their application) excessively harsh and severe. This derives from Draco, an Athenian law scribe under whom small offenses had heavy punishments. Pundit - An expert in a particular subject or field who is frequently called upon to give their opinions to the public.
Posit - Put forward as fact or as basis for argument. Purport - Appear to be or do something, especially falsely.
Refute - Prove (a statement or theory) to be wrong or false; disprove. Rescind - Revoke, cancel, or repeal a law, order or agreement.
Reject - Dismiss as inadequate, unacceptable, or faulty. Renege - Go back on a promise, undertaking, or contract.

item.title: Interesting Words and Phrases 4
item.description:
Aggrandize - Increase the power, status, or wealth of. Enhance the reputation of (someone) beyond what is justified by the facts. Bereave - Be deprived of a loved one through a profound absence especially due to the loved one’s death.
Mania - Mental illness marked by periods of great excitement or euphoria, delusions, and overactivity. An excessive enthusiasm or desire; obsession. Chagrin - Distress or embarrassment at having failed or been humiliated.
Valiant - Possessing or showing courage or determination. Futile - Incapable of producing any useful result; pointless.
Acedia - Spiritual or mental sloth; apathy. Ascetic - Characterized by or suggesting the practice of sever self-discipline and abstention from all forms of indulgence, typically for religious reasons.
Sad - feeling or showing sorrow; unhappy.

item.title: Interesting Words and Phrases 3
item.description:
Depression - Feelings of severe despondency and dejection, typically also with feelings of inadequacy and guilt, often accompanied by lack of energy and disturbance of appetite and sleep. Morbidity - The condition of being diseased. Mortality - The state of being subject to death.
Comorbidity - The simultaneous presense of two chronic diseases or conditions in a patient.
Narrative theory - The study of how stories help people make sense of the world, while also studying how people make sense of stories. Benzodiazepines - Any of a class of heterocyclic organic compounds used as tranquilizers, such as Librium and Valium, often used in treating anxiety.
Opiods - A compound resembling opium in addictive properties or physiological effects. Tricyclic Antidepressant - An early class of drug demonstrated to be effective in treating depression, anxiety, and certain kinds of pain.

item.title: Interesting Words and Phrases 2
item.description:
Accost – Approach and address (someone) boldly or aggressively.

Aflutter – In a state of tremulous excitement.

Apocryphal – (of a story or statement) of doubtful authenticity, although widely circulated as being true.

Commiserate – Express or feels sympathy or pity; sympathize.

Consecrate – Make or declare (something, typically a church) sacred; dedicate formally to a religious purpose.

Countenance – A person’s face or facial expression.

Deference – Polite submission and respect.

item.title: Interesting Words and Phrases 1
item.description:
Acquiesce – Accept something reluctantly but without protest.

Adroit – Clever or skilful.

Amidst - Surrounded by; in the middle of.

Anodyne – Not likely to cause offence or disagreement and somewhat dull.

Antic – grotesque or bizarre.

Aplomb – self-confidence or assurance, especially when in a demanding situation.

Apostasy – The abandonment or renunciation of a religious or political belief or principle.

Asinine – Extremely stupid or foolih.

Assuage – Make (an unpleasant feeling) less intense. Satisfy (an appetite or desire)
